title_private: Dispatch and broadcast: logical tiling versus actual FP16 address route

facts.expected: The requested operation is elementwise maximum with right-aligned broadcast. For P/Q, intended x2 indices are [0,0,0,1,1,1] and the mathematical finite-value result is [3,4,8,7,7,9]. R repeats [3,7,6] across rows and its ideal result is [3,7,8,3,7,9]. Semantic broadcast alone does not prove the selected implementation.

P and R dispatch to KernelMaximumHalfLastAxisBroadcast because dtype is half and sameShape is false. Q dispatches to MaximumScalar<float>. The FP16 dispatch does not validate that only an innermost contiguous x2 row is broadcast.

Same-shape types except int64 use vector KernelMaximumSame. BF16 uses FP32 cast/max/cast; int8 stages through half and float. Int64 always uses scalar, including same shape. Other non-half broadcasts use the stride-based scalar path.

All three tilings have output shape [2,3], rank=2, totalLength=6, sameShape=0, blockNum=1, blockLength=6, tileElements=4096. x1Stride=[3,1]; P/Q x2Stride=[1,0]; R x2Stride=[0,1]. Host allocations use actual input element products.

P specialized path sets row_=3, processes off=0 then 3, and copies count=3 half elements from x2_[off%3]=x2_[0] both times. Actual x2 addresses are indices [0,1,2] per row, not the logical stride mapping. The third half is beyond the 2-element (4-byte) host allocation: requested read [0,6) includes bytes [4,6) outside the allocation.
facts.units: half=2 bytes; x2 read index 2 is outside its physical allocation.

facts.expected: Q reconstructs output coordinates with outShape and zero broadcast strides, obtaining the intended P/Q mapping. R specialized copying [0,1,2] each row fits the actual 3-element x2 allocation and agrees with the supplied finite-value semantic result.

P/R explicitly copy GM->UB on MTE2, use vector Max on V, then copy UB->GM on MTE3 through queues. Q uses scalar index arithmetic and scalar GM loads/comparison/store in this source; it does not invoke vector Max for the broadcast.

SetGlobalBuffer(x2,row_=3) is a tensor view/length assignment, not a host allocation or a broadcast materialization. The current P mismatch is established by concrete requested copy addresses and host bytes, independent of whether a particular device visibly errors.

P/R allocate three half queue slots, 4096*2 bytes each, explicit total 24576 bytes. They operate only count=3 per row; queue storage/tail padding does not enlarge GM x2 allocation or fix broadcast semantics.

No single defined complete P hardware output is supported after the out-of-allocation request. A source-level wrong/missing broadcast guarantee and invalid address range can be concluded; actual exception, hang, adjacent memory content or numerical output requires evidence not present.
